do_not_assume: Saving automatically deploys
A localhost server is reachable
The Rock application name becomes the store name
goal: A deployed application opens in the Rock Mobile Core test shell.
steps: Create the application under Mobile Applications.
Select Flyout or Tabbed navigation unless the use case specifically requires Blank.
Configure an organization-specific alphanumeric API key.
Create or open the homepage.
Add one Content block with minimal valid XAML.
Deploy the application.
Connect the test shell using the Application ID, public API URL and API key.
Launch on at least one target device.
title: Recipe: Create and test a minimal mobile application

do_not_assume: Static content has `CurrentPerson`
Authentication alone establishes block entity context
Valid Lava output is valid XAML
goal: A mobile page displays current, identity-aware or entity-aware content without malformed XAML.
steps: Enable Dynamic Content when fresh server output or `CurrentPerson` is required.
Configure server-side Lava processing and only the Lava commands needed.
For entity context, select the entity type and define the matching page parameter.
Pass the entity GUID through the navigation command.
Handle missing authentication or context explicitly.
Escape all dynamic XAML text.
URL-encode query values.
Test signed-out, signed-in, missing-context and punctuation-heavy records.
Check whether the Content block is static; static Lava has no `CurrentPerson`.
Verify Dynamic Content and Process Lava on Server.
Inspect enabled Lava commands.
Confirm that the shell user is authenticated.
If the block uses entity context, verify the entity type, page parameter name and passed GUID.
Provide a safe missing-context state instead of dereferencing a null entity.
title: Recipe: Build personalized Content block output safely

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A control executes a supported command with a validated parameter.
steps: Check the command’s `M` and `C` requirements.
Confirm whether it needs block or page context.
Start with a minimal button or equivalent control.
Supply the simplest supported parameter form.
If the parameter is structured, use the documented typed object.
If nested controls lose the binding, reference the parent binding context explicitly.
Test the action and its cancellation or failure path.
Move the working command into the final gesture, menu or behavior.
title: Recipe: Add a command-driven interaction

do_not_assume: Removing an expansion suffix preserves expansion
A text replacement proves visual compatibility
A marketing version string matches the runtime shell-version format
Replace only the pattern being tested; do not apply an undifferentiated search-and-replace.
goal: The page renders correctly on .NET MAUI without silently breaking retained older clients.
steps: Record the current and target shell versions.
Inventory migration-sensitive layouts, controls, effects and extensions.
Separate layout, scrolling, sizing, control and styling changes.
Replace deprecated controls only where the target shell supports the replacement.
If both generations must remain active, render only markup compatible with the requesting shell.
Verify the actual shell-version value used by the target environment before writing a version gate.
Deploy the shared content.
Test an old-shell client and a v6+ client separately.
Visually inspect phone and tablet layouts.
Identify the original shell and confirm the target is v6 or later.
Inventory `StackLayout`, expansion options, scrolling containers, hard size requests, `Zone`, `Frame`, `StyledView`, safe-area effects and legacy platform extensions.
Replace only the pattern being tested; do not apply an undifferentiated search-and-replace.
Use constrained grid regions where scrolling or expansion requires them.
Use a v6-compatible border control where appropriate.
Render and visually inspect every affected page on representative phone and tablet layouts.
title: Recipe: Migrate a page from Shell v5 to v6+

do_not_assume: A launcher record proves its selections are correct
A successful check-in proves printing
A generated QR code proves kiosk scanning or printer output
goal: A participant can identify, select, complete check-in and hand labels to a kiosk.
steps: Validate ordinary check-in for the target groups, locations, schedules and configuration.
Confirm HTTPS and geofencing prerequisites.
Create a virtual check-in kiosk device for each distinct campus boundary.
Configure campus geofences and relevant locations.
Configure the launcher’s devices, check-in configuration, theme and valid areas.
Review identity, welcome-back and fallback copy.
Test first-time identification.
Test a recognized returning device.
Test family and individual selection.
Test outside-boundary, closed-window and no-option states.
Complete check-in and scan the QR code at the label kiosk.
Add a selection and verify the updated handoff.
Confirm HTTPS and the geofencing API prerequisite.
Verify location permission and the participant’s current campus or boundary.
Inspect the virtual kiosk device type, campus geofence and associated campus locations.
Confirm that the launcher enables that device.
If campus boundaries differ, confirm separate device records exist.
Test campus selection as well as location-based resolution when the configured experience offers both.
title: Recipe: Prepare mobile check-in

do_not_assume: Provider receipt means store submission
Store submission means approval
Approval means release
Release means the target device installed the update
goal: The publishing provider has a reviewable, secure and complete submission package.
steps: Confirm ownership and active status of the Apple and Google developer accounts.
Complete current account agreements, renewals and verification.
Grant only the publishing access required by the documented process.
Create separate, limited Rock review logins for the two stores.
Confirm the desired shell version and its Core and OS requirements.
Prepare the store name, subtitle, description, categories, support URL, screenshots and graphics.
Resolve Android signing continuity before attempting replacement.
Identify compiled resources and optimize them before submission.
Provide secrets and credentials only through approved secure channels.
Submit through the provider workflow.
Read back submission, review and release status from both stores.
Install the released build and verify its shell version and core journeys.
title: Recipe: Prepare an App Factory publication

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A real target device receives and opens a notification through the intended route.
steps: Verify publishing-time notification configuration.
Confirm the Rock transport, medium and provider configuration.
Request notification permission through the intended app experience.
Confirm the device reports notifications enabled.
Send to a bounded test recipient.
Verify receipt while signed in.
Where required, verify receipt while signed out.
Open the notification and confirm the mobile-page or detail action.
Test both platforms before broad release.
Confirm the app has been through notification-capable publishing configuration.
Verify the Rock communication transport and push medium.
Confirm the provider service-account configuration is current without exposing it.
Check whether the device was asked for permission and whether permission is currently enabled.
Verify the recipient scope and the mobile-page destination.
If using the updated service integration, confirm the applicable Rock Core requirement and provider coordination.
Test actual delivery on both target platforms; a queued communication is not proof of device receipt.
title: Recipe: Validate push notifications

do_not_assume: A provider accepted the job because a request returned successfully
A generated URL points to a complete, public-safe asset
Workflow completion automatically publishes content
goal: Slow processing completes asynchronously and only verified output reaches public mobile content.
steps: Define explicit queued, processing, retry, failed and completed states.
Start the work through a workflow rather than holding the mobile interface open.
Record bounded retry behavior and a terminal failure state.
Poll or receive the provider’s completion result.
Validate the resulting asset.
Link it into mobile or web content only after completion.
Surface failure or review-needed status to an operator.
Check whether the Content block is static; static Lava has no `CurrentPerson`.
Verify Dynamic Content and Process Lava on Server.
Inspect enabled Lava commands.
Confirm that the shell user is authenticated.
If the block uses entity context, verify the entity type, page parameter name and passed GUID.
Provide a safe missing-context state instead of dereferencing a null entity.
title: Recipe: Orchestrate slow media or content work

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Authorized signed-in users can see and complete intended outreach actions, and reminders arrive.
steps: Establish the target Core and Shell versions.
Confirm the mobile feature and pages are installed.
Verify signed-in routing.
Review block settings and data visibility.
Configure or validate assignment days and reminder preferences.
Inspect the jobs that control reminder timing.
Test prayer and connection cadence records.
Complete a touchpoint and confirm history.
Test milestone or pulse behavior that is intentionally enabled.
Verify an actual reminder on a target device.
Confirm the installed Rock and Mobile Shell versions support the intended experience.
Verify the user is signed in.
Confirm page placement and access authorization.
Inspect the relevant block settings and contact-data permissions.
Check onboarding selections, assignment days and reminder preferences.
Verify the configured jobs and their time-of-day values.
Test an actual push notification on the target device.
Stop before treating a scheduled job run as proof of notification delivery.
title: Recipe: Validate Outreach Toolbox for ministry use
